## Instructions for In-Class Tests and Exams

Unless otherwise noted

- Tests are closed book, but you may use **four** letter-sized sheets (both
  sides) of notes (**eight** sheets for the in-class portion of the final); notes must be handwritten
  or typed as you please; no sharing of notes during the test.
- Calculators and other electronic devices are **not** allowed; phones must be
  placed in your bags under your desks or at the front of the room; hands must
  be on top of your desks.
- You are expected to simplify any expressions that can be simplified as even
  numbers, but you may leave other expressions as is, e.g., $\sqrt{47}$ or
  $18/29$.
- You will be provided all of the **critical values** that you need and are
  not expected to memorize them, but you should know how to use them.
- Show all **your work** to justify your answers; answers without adequate
  justification will not receive credit.
- You will be asked to sign an **integrity** statement on the question paper,
  and you are expected to abide by it.
- Students with recognized accommodations will receive the testing
  arrangements specified in their accommodation letters.

## Take-Home Portion of the Final Exam

The take-home portion of the final exam will be **released on Canvas on
November 25, 2026**, the day before Thanksgiving. It contributes **35% of the
final-exam grade**. Submit it by **December 9, 2026, at 8:00 AM
America/Chicago (CST)**, the start of the in-class final.

- There is no time limit other than the submission deadline.
- Submit your files **individually** through the
  [take-home final assignment in Canvas]({{< meta canvas.final_take_home >}}),
  using file uploads. No hard copies are required.
- You may use **AI tools** (e.g., ChatGPT) and other **inanimate resources**.
  You may **not get help from any human**, including classmates, tutors,
  friends, family, or online responders.
- All solutions must be **your own work**. You are responsible for checking
  that AI-generated content is correct and for acknowledging meaningful
  contributions from AI tools or other resources under the course policies.
- Show all **your work** to justify your answers. Answers without adequate
  justification will not receive credit.
- Email clarification questions to
  [hickernell@illinoistech.edu](mailto:hickernell@illinoistech.edu).
  Mathematical help will not be given.
- Sign and date the integrity statement on the exam:

  > I understand these instructions and have not relied on any help for this
  > exam beyond what is allowed, nor provided any help to anyone else beyond
  > what is allowed.

## Archived MATH 565 tests and examinations

Archived assessments are provided for reference. Topics, coverage, and course
emphasis may differ from the current semester. Archived files may contain
errors, and errors found in archived assessments are not eligible for course
extra credit.

```{python}
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.parse import quote
from IPython.display import Markdown, display

root = Path("../assets/tests/archive/565")
pdfs = sorted(root.glob("*.pdf"), key=lambda path: path.name.lower()) \
    if root.exists() else []

if not pdfs:
    display(Markdown("*No archived MATH 565 tests found yet.*"))
else:
    lines = []
    for path in pdfs:
        href = "../assets/tests/archive/565/" + quote(path.name)
        label = path.stem.replace("_", " ")
        lines.append(f"- [{label}]({href})")
    display(Markdown("\n".join(lines)))
```
